doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Playing electric bass with Dion and the Belmonts
summary: Pallo once read bass clef and played Fender bass with a pick for Dion and the Belmonts.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you ever have to play bass?

Yes. That’s with Dion and the Belmonts. We were working this place and they were doing their show. The bass player I was working with couldn’t read. So at that time I was good at reading bass clef so I took his Fender, I guess he had a Fender bass if I recall, and I played the bass part. That was the only time I played the bass. It was easy because the charts were very simple. It was playing on a one and three mostly or something like that, and I could read them off fast. And I played it with a pick on a bass ‘cause boy, that hurts. When you do this on your fingers. But that’s the only time I played a Fender just with that on one of the shows and I tried playing bass but it hurts my fingers number one, if you’re going to use the right, correct way to play it.
